A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TABX simulator and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MARL learning curves, exploration experiments, UED generalization results, value-estimation analyses, and throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds matched-scenario SMAX comparisons, attribute ablations, correlation analyses, competitive policy evaluations, and heuristic-opponent generalization results.

M1.justification: Section 4 changes the stated action space from six actions with one rotation to seven with left/right rotations. However, Appendix A.2 remains unchanged and also lists a no-op action. The PDFs do not establish whether the procedure changed or its description was corrected; the remaining simulator mechanisms and baseline formulations are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on three matched SMAX scenarios: 2s3z, 5m_vs_6m, and 6h_vs_8z. It also introduces learned-policy opponents and UED evaluation across heuristic difficulty tiers from random to expert, substantially broadening the tested interaction conditions beyond v1.

E2.justification: SMAX, previously evaluated against TABX for throughput, becomes a comparator in the matched-scenario learning study in Appendix D. The existing MARL quartet, MAPPO/RND comparisons, and five UED methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 4 and Appendix E extend the main MARL budgets from 20M steps, or 30M for ribbon/grid, to 50M or 100M. New protocols include matched SMAX configurations, throughput measurement without scenario resets, isolated attribute variation, and pairwise policy testing. Appendix E nevertheless retains a contradictory 30M-step sentence. v1 already contained a separate extended ribbon experiment.

E4.justification: v2 adds individual health, speed, and damage ablations in Figure 8; value-error/return correlation analysis in Appendix G; a fixed-configuration throughput control in Appendix H; and heuristic-tier robustness analysis in Appendix J.5. The earlier extended ribbon experiment and RND sensitivity analysis are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The five-seed mean and standard-error convention remains. v2 adds Pearson correlations and significance tests using eight scenario averages and 40 seed-level observations in Figure 25. Appendix J.5 reports three seeds for the new heuristic-tier experiment, despite the general five-seed statement. No increase in replication of existing experiments is established.

E6.justification: New results include matched-SMAX learning curves, competitive payoff matrices showing MAPPO strongest on average, poorer generalization under health-only variation, and correlations of -0.819 and -0.681. Figure 4 extends the main learning curves, while Figure 9 changes throughput curves and count labels; these do not establish same-setting performance gains. Tables 9–11 merely round earlier runtimes up to whole minutes.

T1.justification: The reward definition, PVL/MaxMC formulations, RND objective, and value-error estimation definition are retained. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: TABX provides efficient, configurable battle simulation and supports systematic studies of value learning, exploration, and generalization. The additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 introduces explanations linking UED difficulty to parameter dimensionality, health variation, and curriculum behavior. It qualifies the speed advantage by distinguishing recompilation overhead from simulation cost. A new limitations section identifies combat-only coverage and illustrative empirical insights, while the rewritten impact statement explicitly limits real-world combat interpretations.

D1.justification: The code pointer changes from an anonymous repository to the named GitHub repository. v2 also documents the two-team action/reward interface and how policies are trained for competitive evaluation. Most simulator implementation details, software and hardware disclosures, and hyperparameter Tables 5–8 are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds PettingZoo by Terry et al. and MAgent by Zheng et al. It also strengthens positioning against SMAX by discussing distinct learning dynamics on matched scenarios. The overall related-work organization and benchmark comparison table remain.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section order are preserved. Local expansions explain scenario design and generalization, add competitive evaluation and limitations sections, and introduce new appendix headings. The impact statement is rewritten, acknowledgements are added, and publication information is updated.

P2.justification: Figure 8 expands from two panels to five; Figure 4 receives longer training axes and revised displays; and Figure 9 changes scales and legends. New displays include matched learning curves, correlation plots, fixed-configuration throughput, competitive payoff heatmaps, and heuristic-tier results. Existing appendix figures and tables are also redistributed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of TABX’s distinctiveness and practical tradeoffs through matched-SMAX learning comparisons and a throughput control separating simulation cost from recompilation. Attribute ablations and explicit limitations also make the generalization findings more informative. These gains outweigh remaining reporting problems, including contradictory training budgets in Appendix E and Appendix D’s approximately 2M-step crossover claim where Figure 21 indicates roughly 20M.
